ai.description: This 10–12 cm gecko is pale grey or beige with dark brown crossbands. It features strongly keeled, triangular scales and distinctively bent toes with slender, clawed terminal phalanges.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtopodion scabrum* is best distinguished by the presence of 12–14 longitudinal rows of enlarged, trihedral tubercles on its back, which are notably larger than the interspaces.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtopodion scabrum* inhabits arid, rocky landscapes and human structures in the Indian subcontinent, typically found in low-altitude, sparsely vegetated desert regions.
ai.behavior: The Rough Bent-toed Gecko is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting small insects on vertical surfaces like walls and rocks under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtopodion scabrum* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of one or two eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, generally from spring through summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtopodion scabrum* occurs in arid regions of northwestern India, primarily in Rajasthan and Gujarat, typically inhabiting low-elevation rocky or urban environments.
